examples.ko: 이 우산은 양산 겸용이라서 여름에도 잘 써요.
examples.en: This umbrella doubles as a parasol, so I use it in summer too.

examples.ko: 남녀 겸용 신발이라서 누구나 신을 수 있어요.
examples.en: These are unisex shoes, so anyone can wear them.
This desk is a dual-use one that also works as a dining table.

examples.ko: 겸용은 편하지만 기능마다 조금씩 아쉬울 수 있어요.
examples.en: Dual-purpose items are convenient, but each function can be a little disappointing.

examples.ko: 충전기가 노트북과 휴대폰 겸용으로 나와서 짐이 줄었어요.
examples.en: The charger works for both laptop and phone, so my luggage got lighter.

examples.ko: 겸용 가방이라 백팩으로도 크로스백으로도 들 수 있어요.
examples.en: It's a convertible bag, so you can carry it as a backpack or a crossbody.

explain: '양산 겸용 우산'처럼 두 이름 사이에 넣어 한 물건이 두 가지로 쓰인다고 말해요. 반대로 한 가지 용도만 있으면 '전용'이라고 해요. 사람이나 역할에는 '겸'을 써서 '총무 겸 회계'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: Put it after two names, as in '양산 겸용 우산', to say one object serves two purposes. The opposite, a single purpose only, is '전용'. For people or roles, use '겸' instead, as in '총무 겸 회계'.

examples.ko: 책상 두 개를 나란하게 붙여 놓았어요.
examples.en: I put two desks side by side.
Please line up in two parallel rows.

examples.ko: 두 산줄기가 나란해서 길도 같은 방향으로 나 있어요.
examples.en: The two mountain ridges run in parallel, so the road also runs in the same direction.

examples.ko: 책상이 나란하지 않아서 줄을 다시 맞췄어요.
examples.en: The desks weren't in line, so I lined them up again.

examples.ko: 길과 강이 나란하다고 들어서 쉽게 찾았어요.
examples.en: I heard the road and the river run side by side, so I found it easily.

examples.ko: 두 선이 나란하면 끝까지 만나지 않아요.
examples.en: If two lines are parallel, they never meet.

explain: 대화에서는 '나란히 앉다', '나란히 서다'처럼 '나란히' 모양으로 자주 들려요. 앞뒤가 아니라 옆으로 가지런히 놓이거나 같은 방향으로 이어지는 모양을 말해요. 한 줄로 서는 '일렬로'와는 달라요.

phrases.example: 우리나라 기술이 이제 선진국과 어깨를 나란히 해요.
phrases.en: Our country's technology is now on a par with developed countries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 어깨가 아니라 힘이나 수준이 서로 비슷하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not mean actual shoulders; it means being equal in strength or level.
phrases.en_equiv: stand shoulder to shoulder with; be on a par with

explain_en: In conversation you often hear the form '나란히', as in '나란히 앉다' (sit side by side) and '나란히 서다'. It describes things placed neatly beside each other, or running in the same direction, rather than front to back. It differs from '일렬로', which means in a single line.

examples.en: This coin is made of copper and nickel.

examples.ko: 니켈 알레르기가 있어서 금속 귀걸이를 못 해요.
examples.en: I have a nickel allergy, so I can't wear metal earrings.
A lot of nickel is used in electric car batteries.

examples.ko: 니켈 가격이 오르면서 배터리 값도 올랐대요.
examples.en: I heard battery prices went up as the price of nickel rose.
Stainless steel contains chromium and nickel.

examples.ko: 새로 산 시계가 니켈 도금이라서 반짝반짝해요.
examples.en: My new watch is nickel-plated, so it's really shiny.

explain: 동전, 배터리, 도금, 스테인리스 같은 말과 함께 자주 들어요. 금속 알레르기를 일으키는 금속으로도 잘 알려져 있고, 뉴스에서는 원자재 가격 이야기에 나와요.
explain_en: You often hear it together with coins, batteries, plating and stainless steel. It is also well known as a metal that causes allergies, and in the news it appears in stories about raw material prices.

examples.en: That man has a clean-cut face.

examples.ko: 머리를 자르고 나니 훨씬 멀끔해 보여요.
examples.en: After getting a haircut, you look much neater.
The room looks so tidy after cleaning that I feel good.
I went to the interview dressed neatly.
After I shaved, my face looked clean.
The windows look really clean now that I wiped them.

explain: 사람의 얼굴이나 옷차림이 지저분하지 않고 단정할 때 많이 써요. 물건이나 방이 깨끗하게 정리된 모습에도 쓸 수 있어요. '말끔하다'와 비슷하게 쓰고, 반대말은 '지저분하다'예요.
explain_en: It is often used when a person's face or outfit looks tidy and not messy. You can also use it for things or rooms that are cleaned up. It is used much like '말끔하다', and the opposite is '지저분하다'.

examples.en: After I wiped the floor, it shines glossily.
The marbles were so glossy that I wanted them.
I polished my shoes until they shone and went to the interview.
I picked an apple with a glossy shine.
The railing has been worn smooth and shiny by many hands.
The baby's cheeks are glowing and smooth.

explain: 매끈하고 윤이 나는 모양을 소리처럼 흉내 낸 말이에요. 잘 닦은 물건에도, 오래 만져서 닳은 물건에도 써요. '반들반들'과 비슷하고, '윤이 나다'와 자주 같이 나와요.
explain_en: It imitates the look of a smooth, shiny surface. It works for well-polished things and for things worn smooth by long handling. It is close to '반들반들' and often appears with '윤이 나다'.

examples.en: When sunlight passes through a prism, rainbow colors appear.
We did a prism experiment in science class.
A prism is a triangular shape made of glass.

examples.ko: 책상 위 프리즘이 빛을 여러 색으로 나눠요.
examples.en: The prism on the desk splits light into many colors.
The children made a rainbow with a prism.
The light shining through the prism spread over the wall.

explain: 과학 수업에서 빛을 여러 색으로 나눌 때 나오는 도구예요. '프리즘을 통과하다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고, 관점을 비유하는 글에서 드물게 나와요.
explain_en: The tool in science class that splits light into colors. You say '프리즘을 통과하다'. It is rare in everyday speech and appears only occasionally as a metaphor for a point of view in writing.
